passiveFireProtection.name: Pipe Penetration Sealing
passiveFireProtection.description: The point where a metal pipe passes through a fire-rated wall. Fire Stop systems prevent fire from spreading between compartments and secure the time needed for evacuation.

fireproofingSystems.name: Structural Fireproofing
fireproofingSystems.description: Fire protection for a load-bearing steel column. Early planning and correct application preserve the structural element's load-bearing capacity at high temperatures.

cableProtection.name: Cable Penetration Protection
cableProtection.description: Fire protection for electrical and data cables at floor/wall penetrations. Extends the reliability and service life of the cable materials.

mechanicalSupport.name: Hanger Support System
mechanicalSupport.description: A technical line suspended from the slab above on hanger rods and clamps. Dedicated fixing and support systems carry pipe, duct, and cable runs reliably.

jointSealing.name: Structural Joint Sealing
jointSealing.description: The joint line that allows for the building's structural movement. Fire Stop systems seal these gaps with flexible materials that keep their integrity through expansion and contraction.

acousticInsulation.name: Floor-Wall Acoustic Insulation
acousticInsulation.description: Acoustic insulation at the floor-wall junction that limits sound transmission. Controls both airborne and structure-borne sound paths.

vibrationSolutions.name: Rooftop Equipment Vibration Isolation
vibrationSolutions.description: Rooftop mechanical equipment (generators, engine groups, etc.) mounted on vibration-isolation pads. Prevents equipment-generated vibration from transferring into the structure.

drillingCutting.name: Core Drilling for Pipe Penetration
drillingCutting.description: A precisely sized opening cut into concrete with diamond-tipped equipment for a pipe run. Applied to walls, floors, and other concrete surfaces.

engineeringTesting.name: Facade Anchor Engineering
engineeringTesting.description: Engineering services that secure structural reliability at the curtain-wall anchor point: Support Design, Pull-Out Test, and Load Analysis.

delaySpread.title: Stops Fire Spread
delaySpread.description: Prevents flames from spreading to other areas.

reduceSmoke.title: Blocks Smoke
reduceSmoke.description: Effectively reduces the passage of smoke and toxic gases.

evacuationTime.title: Buys Time
evacuationTime.description: Creates extra time for evacuation, protecting human life.

protectStructure.title: Protects the Structure
protectStructure.description: Protects the building's structure and minimizes material damage.

materials.subtitle: We seal the gaps that protect your building.

cablePenetration.title: Cable penetration
cablePenetration.description: Openings where cable lines pass through a wall are sealed with a suitable firestop system, limiting the spread of fire and smoke to the adjoining space.

metalPipePenetration.title: Metal pipe penetration
metalPipePenetration.description: At wall and floor penetrations for metal pipes, the gap left around the pipe is sealed with a suitable firestop material.

ductPenetration.title: Air duct penetration
ductPenetration.description: At openings where air ducts pass through fire compartments, properly sealing around the penetration limits the spread of fire and smoke between compartments.

plasticPipePenetration.title: Plastic pipe penetration
plasticPipePenetration.description: At plastic pipe penetrations, a suitable passive fire protection solution protects the opening around the pipe in the event of a fire.

step1.title: Zone Division
step1.description: The building is divided into fire compartments to contain the spread of fire.

step2.title: Vertical Isolation
step2.description: Fire walls delay flame spreading to neighboring areas on the same floor.

step3.title: Horizontal Isolation
step3.description: Fire-rated floor and ceiling assemblies stop flame from spreading between floors.

step4.title: Sealing the Penetrations
step4.description: Pipe, cable, and duct penetrations are sealed with Fire Stop systems to keep that protection intact.

processTeaser.heading: This is how Fire Stop protects.
processTeaser.description: Buildings are divided into zones to contain the spread of fire — and that protection is only as strong as how well every small opening in it is sealed.
